First, a function was developed in R.

```{r}
# Importing packages
library(readxl)

# Create folder for saved figures
if (!dir.exists("figures")) {
  dir.create("figures")
}

# Creating function
analyse_roe <- function(file, company_name) {
  
  # Import ROE data
  roe <- read_excel(file)
  
  # Save ROE time-series plot
  png(
    filename = paste0(
      "figures/",
      gsub(" ", "_", company_name),
      "_ROE.png"
    ),
    width = 1600,
    height = 1000,
    res = 200
  )
  
  plot(
    roe$Year,
    roe$ROE,
    type = "l",
    xlab = "Year",
    ylab = "ROE",
    main = paste(company_name, "ROE Time-Series")
  )
  
  dev.off()
  
  # Persistence measures
  # Fit AR(1) model (Take note of how R parameterizes the AR(1) model)
  ar1 <- arima(roe$ROE, order = c(1, 0, 0))
  
  phi <- ar1$coef["ar1"]
  
  mu <- ar1$coef["intercept"]
  
  average <- mean(roe$ROE)
  
  half.life <- (log(0.5)/log(abs(phi)))
  
  # Resilience measures
  # 1) ROE volatility
  
  roe.volatility <- sd(roe$ROE)
  
  
  # 2) Shock severity
  
  shock.threshold <- 1
  
  shock.level <- (mu - shock.threshold*roe.volatility)
  
  roe$Below.Shock <- (roe$ROE < shock.level)
  
  roe$Shock.Episode <- cumsum(roe$Below.Shock & !c(FALSE,roe$Below.Shock[-nrow(roe)]))
  
  roe$Shock.Episode[!roe$Below.Shock] <- NA
  
  shock.results <- aggregate(
    ROE ~ Shock.Episode,
    data = roe,
    FUN = min,
    na.action = na.omit
  )
  
  names(shock.results)[2] <- "Trough.ROE"
  
  shock.results$Severity <- (mu - shock.results$Trough.ROE)
  
  average.max.decline <- mean(shock.results$Severity,na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # 3) Recovery period or Shock duration
  
  recovery.results <- as.data.frame(table(roe$Shock.Episode[!is.na(roe$Shock.Episode)]))
  
  names(recovery.results) <- c("Shock.Episode","Recovery.Period")
  
  average.shock.duration <- mean(recovery.results$Recovery.Period)
  
  recovery.speed <- (1/average.shock.duration)
  
  # Return results
  return(
    data.frame(
      Company = company_name,
      Mean.ROE = average,
      Long.Run.ROE = mu,
      AR1.Phi = phi,
      Half.Life = half.life,
      ROE.Volatility = roe.volatility,
      Shock.Threshold = shock.threshold,
      Shock.Level = shock.level,
      Average.Shock.Severity = average.max.decline,
      Average.Shock.Duration = average.shock.duration,
      Recovery.Speed = recovery.speed
    )
  )
}
```

The function is then applied separately to each company's ROE data.

```{r}
control <- analyse_roe("ControlCompany_ROE.xlsx", "Control_Company")
capitec <- analyse_roe("Capitec_ROE.xlsx","Capitec")
firstrand <- analyse_roe("FirstRand_ROE.xlsx","FirstRand")
shoprite <- analyse_roe("Shoprite_ROE.xlsx","Shoprite")
```

The results from the individual companies are then combined into a single data set for comparison.

```{r}
all.companies <- rbind(
  control,
  capitec,
  firstrand,
  shoprite
)

persistence.resilience.results <- t(all.companies[, -1])
colnames(persistence.resilience.results) <- all.companies$Company
persistence.resilience.results <- as.data.frame(persistence.resilience.results)
print(persistence.resilience.results)
```

The following historical ROE series provide a visual representation of differences in profitability, variability, and in the occurrence of negative shocks across the companies in the sample.

The above graphs highlight the differences in the level and variability in ROE, as well as periods of substantial declines in profitability. However, visual inspection alone does not provide a consistent basis for comparing these characteristics. The time-series are therefore summarized using a set of quantitative measures capturing profitability, persistence and resilience.

(Refer back to the *ROE_analysis* document for an interpretation of the above results.)
